intro_html: Muddy paws, a wet coat, the smell that settles into the fabric. Washable dog beds with covers that come off, so the bed gets cleaned instead of replaced.
description_html:
Every dog bed gets dirty. What matters is what happens next. If the cover won't come off, or fights you going back on, it doesn't get washed, the smell settles in, and the bed goes in the bin while the inside is still fine. A washable dog bed is built so cleaning it is a job you'll actually do on a Sunday afternoon.

What makes a dog bed properly washable

  • A cover that comes right off. The zipped covers on Ullswater, Tetbury, Wensleydale and Loweswater wash at 30°C. Grasmere has a full-zip cover that comes off whole.
  • A core that stays dry. Foam never goes in the machine, so it's worth keeping the wet away from it. Nocturne has a waterproof inner membrane between the cover and the foam, so a spill or a wet coat stays off the foam.
  • A cover that dries. Air-dry fully before refitting. Some labels, such as Loweswater's, say not to tumble dry.

Washable dog beds by how they sleep

Washability shouldn't decide the shape. Start with the dog.

  • If they lean: Ullswater, with four bolstered sides and a non-slip base, up to 127 × 94cm, or Grasmere, a memory foam dog sofa with three cushioned arms, Medium to XXL. More edges are among our bolster dog beds.
  • If they curl and burrow: Loweswater with its sherpa-fleece cushion, XS to XL; Rydal with high cushioned walls and a fleece sleeping surface; or Wensleydale, a deep fibre-filled nest.
  • If they curl first and stretch later: Nocturne, an open-sided bolster bed with egg-crate foam, in 91 × 69cm and 107 × 76cm.
  • If they switch with the seasons: Duddon, 80 × 80cm, with teddy fleece on one face and canvas on the other, best for dogs who curl or lie diagonally.

Fibre or foam, and what that means on wash day

Fibre-filled beds such as Ullswater, Wensleydale, Rydal and Kentmere are soft by design; the cover washes and the bed stays yielding rather than firm. Foam beds like Grasmere, Nocturne and Ennerdale give firmer support; the cover washes, the foam never does. If your dog needs support and comes home wet, choose foam with a waterproof layer.

100 nights, wash days included

A few muddy weeks will tell you whether the wash-day routine works for your house. The beds here come with the 100-night sleep trial: within 100 nights, if it isn't right, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund. One trial per household; damage and other exclusions apply. The Whinlatter car seat in this collection is a travel accessory, so check its returns terms before ordering rather than assuming the trial applies. Free standard UK delivery on orders over £40.

Washable dog bed questions

What temperature should I wash a dog bed cover at?

Whatever its sewn-in label says. Several covers here are listed for 30°C. Air-dry fully before refitting. Our care and washing guide covers drying, smells and when to replace.

Can I put the whole bed in the washing machine?

Not a foam bed: never wash or soak the foam. On fibre-filled beds, wash only the parts the care label allows.

Washable or waterproof: which do I need?

Washable means the mess comes out afterwards. Waterproof means it doesn't get in. For a dog who comes back soaked or has the odd accident, look for both, and see our waterproof dog beds.
